articles.title: How do I install Ironbooks?
articles.summary: Download the Windows installer from the latest release and double-click it. It installs for your Windows user only, with no admin password, and puts an Ironbooks icon on the Desktop and in the Start Menu.

steps.text: Download Ironbooks-Setup-x.y.z.exe from the latest release on GitHub (github.com/RealDealCPA-VR/Ironbooks/releases/latest). The portable Ironbooks-x.y.z.exe runs without installing.
Double-click it. If Windows says "Windows protected your PC", check that the publisher reads RealDealCPA.Ai LLC, then choose More info and Run anyway.
Ironbooks opens when the installer finishes. From then on, use the Ironbooks icon on your Desktop.

notes: macOS and Linux: build it from the source code for now (see INSTALL.md).
Ironbooks keeps itself up to date and asks before it updates. Check by hand with Help > Check for Updates….
asks: set up ironbooks on my computer

articles.title: How do I create a new company?
articles.summary: Choose "Create a new company…" on the start screen (or File > New Company…), pick where the company file is saved, then answer the Setup Interview. Only the company name is required.

steps.text: On the start screen choose "Create a new company…", or in the menu File > New Company….
Choose a name and a folder for the company file, for example "Acme Plumbing.ironbooks" in Documents.
Work through the Setup Interview: Company, Industry, Tax form, Dates, Features, Balances, Finish. Use Back to change an answer; you can skip and fill in the rest later.
On the last step click "Go to Home". A starter Chart of Accounts for your industry is ready.

notes: Run the interview again any time from Help > Run Setup Interview….

articles.title: What is the company file, and how do I open it?
articles.summary: Each company is one file, for example "Acme Plumbing.ironbooks", like a QuickBooks .QBW. Keep it wherever you like: this computer, a USB drive or the office file server.

steps.text: Open it with File > Open or Restore Company… (Ctrl+O), from File > Open Previous Company, or by double-clicking the file.
Ironbooks saves your work into the file a few seconds after each change and when you close it. The title bar says Saved.
Everyone signs in with their own user name and password every time the file is opened. They are stored in the file, so they go wherever it goes.
Copy it, back it up or send it to your accountant like any other file, or use "Save a copy…".

articles.title: How do I find a screen or a task quickly?
articles.summary: Press Ctrl+K anywhere and type what you want to do in plain words, such as "I got paid" or "pay a bill". The search box above the menu finds any screen by its name or its QuickBooks name.

steps.text: Press Ctrl+K and type the task. Pick the suggestion and the right screen opens, often with the form already started.
Or type in the search box at the top of the left menu. It knows QuickBooks names too, for example "Finance Charges".
Press ? on any page for the keyboard shortcuts. The round ? bubble beside a page title explains what that page is for.
Still stuck? Open Help & Glossary, or click Ask AI in the top bar and ask in your own words.

articles.title: Where are all the other screens? (Simple and All menus)
articles.summary: The left menu has two styles. Simple shows only everyday tasks. All menus shows every screen, grouped like the QuickBooks menus. Switch with the Simple / All menus control at the top of the menu.

steps.text: At the top of the left menu, click "All menus" (or "Show all menus…" at the bottom of the Simple menu). Click "Simple" to go back.
The same choice is "Menu style" in My Preferences, where All menus is called Advanced.
In either style, search (Ctrl+K or the menu search box) reaches every screen.

notes: A screen can also be missing because its feature is switched off in Preferences, or because your role may not open it.
asks: i cannot find a menu item

articles.title: How do I turn a feature on or off (payroll, inventory, sales tax…)?
articles.summary: Features are switched in Preferences. A feature that is off is hidden from the menus. The Setup Interview sets them when the company is made.

steps.text: Open Preferences and pick the category on the left, for example Payroll & Employees.
Open the Company Preferences tab, change the setting and save.
Or run the Setup Interview again and change your answers on the Features step.

notes: Only someone who may change company settings can switch features.

articles.title: What should I work on first each day?
articles.summary: Open "Needs attention". It lists everything waiting on you, most urgent first: bank lines to sort, late customers, bills due, reconciling, payroll taxes, to-dos and backups.

steps.text: Open Needs attention and work down the list.
Use the button on each line (Sort it, Send reminder, Pay, Done). Not now? Choose Later to snooze or dismiss it.
Home shows the same list plus an Overview of how money moves. Click any step there to do it.

articles.title: How do I enter opening balances?
articles.summary: The Setup Interview has a Balances step: enter what each bank, credit card, loan and other account held on your start date. Moving from QuickBooks? Import your history instead and the balances come with it.

steps.text: Open the Setup Interview and go to the Balances step.
Check the "Balances as of" date, then add each account and its balance with "Add an account".
Finish the interview. Ironbooks records the balances as one opening entry.
Coming from QuickBooks: use Migrate from QuickBooks, which brings in your accounts, history and open invoices and bills.

articles.title: How do I create an invoice?
articles.summary: Use Invoices to bill a customer who will pay you later. Saving the invoice records the sale and what the customer owes you.

steps.text: Open Invoices and click "New Invoice" (Ctrl+I).
Pick the customer, then add a line for each thing you sold: the item, quantity and rate.
Check the date, terms and total, then save. The amount now shows as owed by the customer.
To email or print it, save it marked to be emailed or printed, then use Print & Send Forms.

notes: Paid on the spot? Use a Sales Receipt instead: no invoice is needed.

articles.title: I got paid. How do I record it?
articles.summary: It depends on whether you sent an invoice first.

steps.text: You sent an invoice: use Receive Payments, pick the customer, enter the amount and tick the invoices it pays.
No invoice (paid on the spot): use a Sales Receipt.
When you take the money to the bank, use Make Deposits so your books show the same deposit as your bank statement.

asks: apply a payment to an invoice

articles.title: How do I record a sale that was paid right away?
articles.summary: Use a Sales Receipt when the customer pays on the spot by cash, card or check, so no invoice is needed.

steps.text: Open Sales Receipts and click "New Sales Receipt".
Pick the customer, add what you sold and how they paid, then save.
Deposit the money with Make Deposits when it goes to the bank.

articles.title: How do I give a customer a quote and turn it into an invoice?
articles.summary: An estimate is a price quote. It does not change your books until you turn it into an invoice.

steps.text: Open Estimates and click "New Estimate". Pick the customer, add the work or items and an expiration date, and send it to the customer.
When the customer says yes, click Accept on the estimate, then "Convert to Invoice".
Billing in stages? Use "Create Progress Invoice" and bill a percentage of the estimate, or chosen quantities or amounts. The estimate keeps track of what is already invoiced and what remains.
Estimate Follow-up lists quotes that are still waiting for an answer.

articles.title: How do I give a customer a credit or a refund?
articles.summary: A credit memo lowers what a customer owes you, for a return or a mistake. You can apply it to an invoice or refund the money.

steps.text: Open Credit Memos and click "New Credit Memo".
Pick the customer and add what you are crediting, then save.
On the credit memo, click "Apply Credit" to take it off an open invoice, or "Record Refund" to pay the money back from a bank account.

articles.title: How do I see who owes me money, and follow up?
articles.summary: The A/R Aging report shows each customer, what they owe and how late it is. Collect overdue payments is where you follow up.

steps.text: Open A/R Aging to see every customer balance by how overdue it is.
Open Collect overdue payments to log a call, email the overdue invoices or a statement, or print a collection letter.
Money coming in shows estimates, unbilled work, open and overdue invoices in one view.

notes: You can also ask Ask AI "Who owes us money?" for the totals.

articles.title: How do I send a customer a statement?
articles.summary: Customer Statement lists a customer’s charges, payments and balance for a period, one at a time or for every customer with a balance.

steps.text: Open Customer Statement.
Choose the Format (Balance Forward or Open Item), the customer and the dates, then view it.
For everyone at once, use "Batch — all customers with balances" and choose Combined PDF or ZIP (one PDF per customer).
To email one statement, use "Email a customer statement" on Print & Send Forms.

articles.title: How do I email or print invoices and other forms?
articles.summary: Print & Send Forms holds everything marked "To be emailed" or "To be printed", so you send or print it in one go. Email needs your mail server set up once.

steps.text: Set up email once in Preferences > Send Forms (the mail server that sends your forms).
Open Print & Send Forms.
Under "To be emailed", tick the forms and click "Send selected". Under "To be printed", tick them and click "Print selected".

notes: The name and address your forms are sent from, and "Bcc me", are in My Preferences.

articles.title: How do I add a customer or a job?
articles.summary: Customers lists everyone you sell to, with their details, balance and history. A job is a project under a customer.

steps.text: Open Customers and click "Add Customer". Fill in the name and contact details and save.
For a project you track separately, add a job under the customer.
Adding many at once? Use Add/Edit Multiple and paste them from a spreadsheet.

notes: You can also type a new name straight into an invoice and add it from there.

articles.title: How do I invoice many customers the same thing?
articles.summary: Invoice many customers sends the same charge, for example a monthly fee, to a group of customers in one go.

steps.text: Open Invoice many customers.
Pick the customers (or a saved Billing Group) and add the items once.
Create the invoices, then send them from Print & Send Forms.

articles.title: How do I charge late fees or interest?
articles.summary: Late-payment charges adds interest or a late fee to customers whose invoices are overdue.

steps.text: Open Late-payment charges.
Check the rate and grace period, review the list, then assess the charges you want.

articles.title: How do I set up, charge and pay sales tax?
articles.summary: Add a sales tax item for each rate you charge and the agency it is paid to. Invoices and sales receipts then add the tax, and Pay Sales Tax sends what you collected to each agency.

steps.text: Open Sales tax items and click "New sales tax item". Give it a name and a rate, and pick (or add) its tax agency.
Charge it on invoices and sales receipts. The Sales Tax Liability report shows what you owe each agency.
To pay: open Pay Sales Tax, pick the bank account and the "show tax due through" date, tick the agencies and pay.

notes: Sales tax must be switched on in Preferences for these screens to show.
asks: how much sales tax do i owe

articles.title: How do I put my logo on invoices or change how they look?
articles.summary: Form Templates sets the logo, colors and fields on your invoices and other printed forms.

steps.text: Open Form Templates.
Pick the form, add your logo, choose the colors and the fields to show, then save.

articles.title: How do I enter and pay a vendor bill?
articles.summary: Two ways, depending on when you pay. Pay later: enter the bill now and pay it from Pay Bills. Pay now: write a check.

steps.text: Pay later: open Enter Bills, click "New Bill", pick the vendor, the amount and what it was for.
When you pay: open Pay Bills, tick the bills, choose the bank account and payment date, then pay.
Pay now (check, debit card or cash): use Write Checks instead.

notes: A bill entered in Enter Bills must be paid in Pay Bills, not with Write Checks, or the vendor still shows as owed.

articles.title: How do I record something I paid for right away?
articles.summary: Write Checks records money you paid right away by check, debit card or cash, and what it was for.

steps.text: Open Write Checks (Ctrl+W).
Pick the bank account, the payee and the expense account, and enter the amount. The payee can be a vendor or someone on the Other Names list.
Save. To print it later, mark it "to be printed" and use Print Checks.

notes: Many at once? Type them into the account’s register, or paste them into Enter many transactions.

articles.title: How do I record credit card charges?
articles.summary: Enter each charge on Enter Credit Card Charges, type them into the card’s register, or import the card statement and review the lines like a bank account.

steps.text: One charge: open Enter Credit Card Charges (menu: Banking > Enter Credit Card Charges). Pick the card, the payee, the expense account and the amount.
Several: open Registers and pick the credit card account. Type a row and press Enter: it saves as a card charge.
A whole statement: import the card statement file and review the lines.
Reconcile the card against its statement. At the end you can write a check for the balance.

notes: A credit card must be set up as a Credit Card account, not a bank account, or its amounts show the wrong way round.

articles.title: How do I print checks?
articles.summary: Print Checks prints the checks you marked "to be printed" on your check stock: voucher, 3 per sheet or wallet.

steps.text: Open Print Checks.
First time: open Printer Setup and choose the check paper and check style, and where the check sits on the page.
Pick the Bank Account and the Next Check Number, tick the checks and print.
Answer "Did checks print OK?" so the check numbers are recorded.

notes: Paychecks and customer refund checks can be added to the same queue from this screen.
asks: checks print in the wrong place

articles.title: How do I record a credit or refund from a vendor?
articles.summary: A vendor credit lowers what you owe a vendor, for a return or an overcharge. You use it when you pay their bills.

steps.text: Open Vendor Credits and click "New Vendor Credit". Pick the vendor, the date and the account or item, and the amount.
On the credit, click "Apply Credit" and pick the bill it reduces. The vendor sent the money back instead? Click "Record Refund" and choose the bank account it went into.
Pay what is left of the bill in Pay Bills.

articles.title: How do I order from a vendor and receive the items?
articles.summary: A purchase order is an order you send a vendor. It does not change your books until the items arrive or the bill comes.

steps.text: Open Purchase Orders and click "New Purchase Order". Pick the vendor and the items you are ordering.
Items arrived before the bill: open Receive Items, pick the vendor and the purchase order, and enter what arrived.
When the bill comes: open Bill for received items, pick the vendor and the item receipt, check the amounts and save.

asks: receive items against a purchase order

articles.title: How do I turn a receipt photo into an expense?
articles.summary: Drop a receipt photo or PDF anywhere in the app. Ironbooks reads it on this computer and fills in a new expense or bill for you to check.

steps.text: Drag a receipt anywhere in the app, or open Receipts and click "Add receipts".
From your phone: click "Send from your phone", make a phone link and scan the code with your phone’s camera. Take a photo of each receipt and tap Send.
Open each receipt in the list, check what was read and save it as an expense or a bill.

notes: Reading uses built-in text recognition. A local AI model can read photos too: see "How receipts are read" on the Receipts screen.
The phone must be able to reach this computer (the same network or your tailnet).
asks: send a receipt from my phone

articles.title: How do I add a vendor?
articles.summary: Vendors lists everyone you buy from, with their details, the balance you owe and history.

steps.text: Open Vendors and click "Add Vendor". Fill in the name and details and save.
Paying a contractor you will send a 1099? Enter their tax ID on the vendor.

articles.title: How do I prepare 1099s for contractors?
articles.summary: The 1099 Worksheets total what you paid each vendor for the year, by box, from the expense accounts you map.

steps.text: Open the 1099 Worksheets and choose the Calendar Year.
Under "Account-to-Box Mapping", choose which expense accounts count toward each box, then "Save Mapping".
Check the list. "Not on file" under Tax ID means the vendor still needs one. "Download CSV" exports the figures.
1099 E-File prepares the file for filing.

notes: Check the figures against current IRS rules before filing.

articles.title: How do I bring in my bank transactions?
articles.summary: Import the statement file your bank gives you: PDF, a scan or phone photo, Excel, CSV, OFX or QBO. There is no bank login. Every row is checked against the statement’s balances before it is brought in.

steps.text: Open Bank Feeds / Import and choose "Import a statement file", or drop the file onto the window. In the menu: File > Import Bank File….
Choose the bank or credit card account the statement belongs to and check the rows that were read.
Import, then review each line.

notes: Ironbooks never connects to your bank. You download the statement from the bank’s website and import the file.
No file? Type the transactions into the account’s register, or paste them into Enter many transactions.
asks: import a csv from my bank

articles.title: How do I categorize the bank lines I imported?
articles.summary: Review bank transactions shows each imported line with a suggested match or account. You confirm, change or exclude it.

steps.text: Open Review bank transactions and pick the Bank Account.
For each line under To Review: "Confirm Match" when it matches something you already entered, or "Use suggestion" to add it to the suggested account. Pick another account if the suggestion is wrong.
Not sure about a line? "Ask AI" asks your connected model to pick an account. You still confirm.
"Apply Rules" runs your bank rules; "Auto-add Suggested" adds every line whose suggestion is sure enough.
A line that is not yours, or a duplicate: Exclude it.

articles.title: How do I make bank lines categorize themselves?
articles.summary: A bank rule tells Ironbooks which account to use for bank lines that look alike, such as every SHELL OIL charge going to Fuel. It also offers a rule when you repeat a choice.

steps.text: Open Bank rules and click "New rule".
Under "When a bank line…", say what the description contains. Under "Then put it in…", choose the account.
Click "Test on recent lines" to see what it would catch, choose Suggest or Add automatically, then "Save rule".
Under "Rules we can make for you", accept the rules Ironbooks offers from choices you repeated.

articles.title: How do I reconcile a bank or credit card account?
articles.summary: Reconciling checks your books against the statement, so you know every transaction is right. Do it when each statement arrives.

steps.text: Open Reconcile, choose the account, and enter the Statement Date and Statement Ending Balance. Click "Start Reconciliation".
Tick each transaction that appears on the statement ("Mark All" ticks everything). Enter any service charge or interest when asked.
When Difference is 0.00, click "Finish Reconciliation".
Something missing? Add it, or import the statement, then come back: an unfinished reconciliation can be resumed.

notes: A small difference you cannot find can be closed with "Finish with Adjustment".
Past reconciliations and their reports are under Reconciliation History on the same screen.

articles.title: How do I undo or redo a reconciliation?
articles.summary: Undo Last Reconciliation un-ticks the latest reconciliation for an account, so you can do it again.

steps.text: Open Reconcile and choose the account.
Click "Undo Last Reconciliation" and confirm. Repeat to go back further, one statement at a time.
The Reconciliation Discrepancy report shows reconciled transactions that were changed afterwards.

articles.title: How do I record a bank deposit?
articles.summary: Make Deposits groups the customer payments you took to the bank into one deposit, so it matches your bank statement.

steps.text: Open Make Deposits.
Choose the bank account under "Deposit To" and tick the payments you deposited under "Payments in Undeposited Funds".
Other money in (a loan, an owner contribution): "Add Line" with the account it belongs to. Kept some cash? Tick "Take cash back from this deposit".
Click "Make Deposit".

notes: Payments wait in Undeposited Funds until they are put on a deposit.

articles.title: How do I move money between my own accounts?
articles.summary: Transfer Funds moves money between your own accounts, for example checking to savings.

steps.text: Open Transfer Funds and click "New Transfer".
Pick the From Account and the To Account, the amount and the date, then save.

articles.title: How do I add a bank or credit card account?
articles.summary: Bank accounts lists your bank and credit card accounts with their balances. Each one is also an account in the Chart of Accounts.

steps.text: Open Bank accounts and add a new account.
Choose the right type: a checking or savings account is a Bank account, a card is a Credit Card account.
Enter its balance on your start date in the Setup Interview, or import its history.

articles.title: How do I see or type transactions in a register?
articles.summary: A register shows every transaction in one account, like a checkbook, with a running balance. You can type new rows straight into it.

steps.text: Open Registers and pick an account (Ctrl+R).
Type a row and press Enter. It saves as the right check, deposit, transfer, card charge or journal entry.
A new payee asks whether it is a Customer, Vendor, Employee or Other, right there.

asks: see all transactions in an account

articles.title: How do I enter or paste many transactions at once?
articles.summary: Enter many transactions is a spreadsheet-style grid for checks, deposits, card charges, bills, invoices or journal entries. Each row is checked as you go and saved as its own transaction.

steps.text: Open Enter many transactions and pick the transaction type.
Type rows, or paste them from Excel or Google Sheets.
Fix the rows marked red, then save.

articles.title: How do I track a loan and its payments?
articles.summary: Loans tracks what you owe, each payment and how much of it is interest. "What if" compares another rate, payment or term.

steps.text: Open Loans and click "Add a Loan". Enter its amount, rate and term. Tick "already being paid" if you have been paying it.
Set up each payment. Ironbooks splits it between principal and interest.

articles.title: How do I add or change an account (category)?
articles.summary: The Chart of Accounts is the list of categories your money is sorted into: bank accounts, income, expenses, what you own and owe.

steps.text: Open the Chart of Accounts (Ctrl+A) and click "Add Account".
Choose the type and detail type, give it a name, and pick a tax line if your accountant uses one. Save.
An account you no longer use: make it inactive instead of deleting it, so its history stays.

notes: Any account picker also offers "Set Up" for a name it does not know, so you can add the account without leaving the form.

articles.title: How do I make a journal entry?
articles.summary: A journal entry moves amounts between accounts directly. It is mostly used by accountants for adjustments. Debits must equal credits.

steps.text: Open Journal entries and click "New Journal Entry".
Add a line for each account with a debit or a credit. A line on Accounts Receivable needs the customer in the Name column; a line on Accounts Payable needs the vendor.
Save. The form will not save until debits equal credits.

notes: Not an accountant? Most things have their own screen (invoice, bill, check, transfer). Use those first.
Ask AI can draft a journal entry for you to approve: ask it to "record…" and review the proposed entry.

articles.title: How do I close the month?
articles.summary: Close the month is a guided checklist: reconcile, tidy up, review balances, then lock the books with a closing date and download a report pack.

steps.text: Open Close the month and pick the "Month to close".
Work through each step. Use "Mark as reviewed", or "Skip this step…" with a reason.
Click "Close the books" and set the closing date password. Transactions dated on or before the closing date can then be changed only with that password.
Click "Download report pack (PDF)".

notes: The closing date can also be set on its own in Preferences ("Set Closing Date").

articles.title: How do I close the year?
articles.summary: Year-End Close moves the year’s net income into Retained Earnings with one closing entry.

steps.text: Finish and close the last month of the year first.
Open Year-End Close, enter the Fiscal Year and confirm.
To reverse it, void the closing entry it created.

notes: Reports work without this step: they show prior-year profit as Retained Earnings on their own. Ask your accountant whether they want the closing entry.

articles.title: How do I send my books to my accountant?
articles.summary: Send the whole file, a ledger export, or an Accountant’s Copy that lets your accountant fix an earlier period while you keep working.

steps.text: A copy of everything: File > Save Copy As…, or File > Create Portable Company File… for a smaller file to email.
Just the numbers: File > Export Shareable Ledger, as an Excel Workbook or a PDF Summary.
Both working at once: open Accountant’s Copy, pick the dividing date and create the copy. When the changes file comes back, open it there, check each change, then import.

notes: For an auditor who should see only one period, use Period Copy.
asks: send my books to my accountant
share the file with my bookkeeper

articles.title: How do I track income and expenses by department, location or class?
articles.summary: Classes & locations lets you tag each transaction line, then report profit for each tag.

steps.text: Open Classes & locations and click "Add Class" (or "Add Location") for each one.
Pick the class on the lines of invoices, bills, checks and journal entries.
Run Profit & Loss by class.

articles.title: How do I make a budget or forecast?
articles.summary: Budgets holds a target (or a forecast) by account and month, and compares it with what actually happened.

steps.text: Open Budgets and click "New Budget". Give it a name and fiscal year and choose what you are planning.
Type the monthly amounts, or use "Create from actuals" to start from a past year.
Open the budget to see Actual, Budget and Variance side by side.

articles.title: How do I make a transaction repeat (rent, subscriptions)?
articles.summary: Recurring transactions saves a transaction you enter again and again, so it repeats on a schedule or with one click.

steps.text: Enter the transaction once, then save it as recurring from its form (Ctrl+M memorizes it).
Open Recurring transactions and set how often it repeats.

articles.title: How do I see who changed or deleted something?
articles.summary: The Audit Trail records every change: who made it, when, and the values before and after. It cannot be switched off.

steps.text: Open the Audit Trail and filter by Action, Entity Type and dates. Click a line to see the values before and after.
For voided and deleted transactions only, open the Voided/Deleted Transactions report.

articles.title: How do I track equipment and depreciation?
articles.summary: Fixed Assets lists the equipment, vehicles and other things the business owns for more than a year, with their cost, and posts straight-line depreciation for you.

steps.text: Open Fixed Assets and click "Add Asset". Enter the Asset Name, Cost, Salvage Value, Useful Life (months) and the Placed in Service date.
Each period, click Depreciate on the asset, check the Monthly Amount and the Depreciation Date, then "Post Depreciation".
Schedule shows every period and which ones are posted.

notes: Depreciation here is straight-line: (Cost - Salvage) / Useful Life per month. For another method, post the journal entry your accountant gives you.

articles.title: How do I set up payroll and add employees?
articles.summary: Turn payroll on, add each employee with their pay rate and tax settings, then enter anything already paid this year.

steps.text: Turn payroll on in Preferences > Payroll & Employees.
Open Employees & payroll and add each employee.
Open Payroll Setup for payroll items, state payroll taxes and, if you start mid-year, the year-to-date amounts already paid.

notes: Ironbooks works out paychecks and taxes and gives you the form figures. It does not file taxes or move money for you. Check tax tables against current rules.

articles.title: How do I pay my employees?
articles.summary: Run payroll works out each paycheck, the taxes withheld and what you owe the government.

steps.text: Open Run payroll and click "New Pay Run".
Enter the Pay Date and the Period Start and Period End, and pick the employees. "Pull time" brings in hours from Time Tracking.
Check the paychecks, then click "Run Payroll".
Print the checks or the pay stubs.

articles.title: How do I pay payroll taxes?
articles.summary: Pay payroll taxes records the payment of the taxes you withheld and owe to the government.

steps.text: Open Pay payroll taxes.
Under "Pay Payroll Liabilities by Item", pick what you are paying, the Payment Date and the Payment Account, then "Record Payment".
Make the actual payment to the agency yourself: Ironbooks records it, it does not send it.

articles.title: Where do I get W-2, 941 and 940 figures?
articles.summary: Payroll Forms downloads the W-2, W-3, Form 941 and Form 940 figures from the payroll you ran.

steps.text: Open Payroll Forms.
Pick the form, the employee or quarter and the Tax Year, then download it.
Payroll Reports shows the totals behind the forms.

notes: Verify the figures against current regulations before filing.

articles.title: How do I track hours worked?
articles.summary: Time Tracking records hours by employee, and by customer or job when you bill for time.

steps.text: Open Time Tracking and click "Log Time". Pick the employee, the hours and, for billable work, the customer, service item and rate.
To bill the customer: "Create Invoice from Billable Time" on the same screen.
To pay the hours: in a pay run, click "Pull time".

articles.title: How do I add a product or service I sell?
articles.summary: Items are the products and services you buy and sell. Each item knows its price and which account it goes to.

steps.text: Open Items and click "Add Item".
Choose the kind: Service, Inventory (a product you keep in stock), Non-Inventory, Bundle (group), Other Charge or Discount. Then enter the name, Sales Price and income account.
Pick the item on invoices, sales receipts, purchase orders and bills.

articles.title: How do I correct inventory after a count?
articles.summary: Adjust inventory records a physical count or a change in value, and posts the difference to the ledger for you.

steps.text: Open Adjust inventory.
Physical Count: pick the item, enter the Counted Quantity and Count Date, then "Record Count". Batch Count does many items from a worksheet.
Value Adjustment changes what the stock is worth without changing the quantity.

articles.title: How do I see what I have in stock and what it is worth?
articles.summary: The Inventory Center shows each item’s quantity on hand; Inventory Valuation shows what the stock is worth.

steps.text: Open the Inventory Center for quantities, reorder points and each item’s activity.
Open Inventory Valuation for the value of what is on hand.

asks: how much stock do i have
what do i need to reorder

articles.title: How do I build a product from parts?
articles.summary: Build products turns component items into a finished item, using its bill of materials.

steps.text: Add the finished product and its parts as items.
Open Build products and pick the product under "Select Assembly Item". Under Bill of Materials, "Add Component" for each part with its quantity per assembly, then "Save BOM".
Under Build / Unbuild, enter the Quantity and build. "Queue as Pending" holds a build until the parts are in stock; Finalize it from Pending Builds.

articles.title: How do I give some customers different prices?
articles.summary: Customer Pricing sets a special price for one customer on one item; Pricing rules changes prices automatically, for example 10% off for a group or a sale price for a date range.

steps.text: Open Customer Pricing and click "Set Price". Pick the customer and the item and enter the Custom Price.
Open Pricing rules and click "New rule" for automatic changes: who and what it applies to, and the price change.

asks: give a discount to a customer

articles.title: How do I see whether I made money?
articles.summary: Profit & Loss shows money in minus money out for a period. The Balance Sheet shows what the business owns and owes on one date.

steps.text: Open Profit & Loss and choose the dates at the top.
Click any amount to see the transactions behind it.
Compare periods with Profit & Loss comparison or by month.
Open the Balance Sheet for what you own and owe.

notes: Or ask Ask AI "How did we do this month?" for the totals in a sentence.

articles.title: Where is the report I need?
articles.summary: The Report Center lists every report: profit, what you own and owe, sales, spending, taxes, payroll and more.

steps.text: Open the Report Center and click a report to open it.
Know its name, or its QuickBooks name? Press Ctrl+K and type it.
A report you use often: save it with your settings and find it under Saved reports.
Nothing fits? Build your own in Report Builder.

articles.title: How do I find a transaction?
articles.summary: Find Transactions searches by type, name, account, date, amount, number or memo.

steps.text: Open Find Transactions (Ctrl+F).
Set any filters, for example the amount range and the dates, and click Find.
Click a result to open the transaction.

notes: Ask AI also searches posted transactions: try "find the payment to Staples in March".

articles.title: How do I see what I owe vendors?
articles.summary: A/P Aging shows each vendor, what you owe and how overdue it is.

steps.text: Open A/P Aging.
Pay what is due from Pay Bills.

articles.title: How do I see what a number on a report is made of?
articles.summary: Click any amount on a report to see every transaction that adds up to it, with the same dates and filters.

steps.text: Open the report, for example Profit & Loss.
Click the amount. Then click a date to open that transaction and its original document.
Use Back to return to the report where you left it.

asks: what is this number made of
see the transactions behind a total

articles.title: How do I back up my books?
articles.summary: Back Up & Restore keeps safe copies of your company file, automatically on a schedule and whenever you ask.

steps.text: Open Back Up & Restore (File > Back Up Company…).
Under "Automatic backups", choose how often, how many to keep, and a Backup folder on a USB drive or another disk. Click "Save settings".
Click "Back up now" to make a copy today.

notes: Keep backups on a different disk from the company file. A backup on the same disk does not survive that disk failing.
You can also copy the .ironbooks file itself while it is closed in Ironbooks.

articles.title: How do I restore a backup?
articles.summary: Pick a backup from the history, look inside it to be sure it is the one you want, then restore.

steps.text: Open Back Up & Restore and find the backup under "Backup history".
Click "Look inside & restore…" to see what the copy holds before you choose it.
Restore. Ironbooks first makes a safety copy of the books as they are now.
No company open (a new computer): on the start screen choose "Open or restore a company file…" and pick the backup file.

notes: Restoring replaces the current books with the backup. Anything entered since that backup is not in it.

articles.title: How do I move my books to another computer?
articles.summary: Your books are one file. Install Ironbooks on the other computer and open the same file there.

steps.text: On the old computer, see where the file is: Company File > "Show in folder". Close the company (File > Close Company).
Copy the .ironbooks file to the new computer, by USB drive or your network.
Install Ironbooks there and choose "Open or restore a company file…". Sign in with the same user name and password.

notes: Two people at once? Do not pass copies back and forth: put the file on a shared drive or use multi-user mode.
asks: transfer my books to another pc

articles.title: How do I add a user and limit what they can do?
articles.summary: Users & Roles sets who can sign in to this company file and what each person may do. A role sets access per activity, such as Invoices or Receive Payments.

steps.text: Open Users & Roles and click "Add user". Enter their name, login and a password, and give them one or more roles.
Built-in roles cannot be changed: use "Clone role" to make your own version, then tick what it allows.
View Permissions compares what each role or user may do, side by side.

notes: Users and their passwords are stored in the company file, so they go wherever the file goes.
asks: limit what an employee can see
reset a password for a user

articles.title: How do I protect my company file with a password?
articles.summary: A protected company file is encrypted. Only its user names and passwords, or its recovery key, open it, on any computer.

steps.text: An Admin opens Security and clicks "Protect This Company File with Passwords".
Print or save the recovery key and keep it somewhere safe. It is the way back in if passwords are forgotten.
For a second step at sign-in, set up Two-Factor Authentication on the same screen with an authenticator app, and save the recovery codes.

articles.title: I forgot my password. How do I get back in?
articles.summary: On the sign-in screen choose "I forgot my password", or use the file’s recovery key. An Admin can also reset your password.

steps.text: On the sign-in screen click "I forgot my password" and answer your challenge question, or click "Use the recovery key".
Or ask an Admin: in Users & Roles they open your user and choose "Reset password".
Lost the phone with your authenticator app? Type one of your recovery codes instead of the code.

notes: To change a password you still know, open Change My Password.

articles.title: How do several people work in the same company file?
articles.summary: Put the company file on a shared drive and open it from any computer. While someone is in it, it is locked to them, the way QuickBooks single-user mode works, until they let others in.

steps.text: Add a user name for each person.
If someone else has the file open, Ironbooks tells you who and on which computer, and offers Ask to Come In.
They choose Let Them In (you both work at once, multi-user mode), Hand It Over (they close it and it opens for you) or Not Now.
To let people join without asking, the person in the file chooses File > Switch to Multi-user Mode.
The first time a computer lets others in, Windows may ask whether Ironbooks can use the network: choose Allow on private networks.

notes: Working from outside the office: host over your Tailscale tailnet with "Host on Tailscale" on the Multi-user screen, and give the other person the connection code.
asks: two people at the same time
someone else has the file open

articles.title: Can I try something without changing my real books?
articles.summary: Yes. "Try it on a copy" opens Ironbooks on a throwaway copy of your whole company file (the sandbox). An orange SANDBOX bar shows on every page and anything you print is stamped SANDBOX.

go.label: Try it on a copy
go.menu: Setup › Try it on a copy

steps.text: Click "Try it on a copy". The copy opens straight away.
Practice or test anything. Emails, bank feeds, scheduled reports and automatic backups are off in the sandbox, so nothing leaves the copy.
When you are done: discard the sandbox (the copy is deleted) or keep it as a training file with a name you choose. Nothing is ever copied back into your real books.

articles.title: What leaves my computer, and how do I control it?
articles.summary: Your books stay on this computer. Privacy & Network lists every service that could send anything out; each one is off until you turn it on.

steps.text: Open Privacy & Network.
Choose the Network mode: Offline, Local network + tailnet (recommended), or Allow cloud services I choose.
Under "What could leave this computer", turn on only the services you want. "Recent network activity" shows what was allowed or blocked.

notes: Update checks (app version and platform only) are the one connection on by default, and you can turn them off here.

articles.title: Where are the settings?
articles.summary: Preferences holds settings for the whole company; My Preferences holds your own, such as the menu style, the address your forms are sent from, and light or dark appearance.

steps.text: Company-wide settings: open Preferences, pick a category on the left, change what you need and save.
Just for you: open My Preferences.
AI models and automation have their own screen.

articles.title: How do I connect an AI model?
articles.summary: Open AI & Automation and pick one of two choices: a free model on this computer (nothing leaves your PC), or your ChatGPT Plus or Pro plan (sign in in your browser; no API key and no extra bill). You can use both.

steps.text: Open AI & Automation (Company > AI & Automation).
Free, on this computer: click "Set up free AI on this computer". On Windows Ironbooks installs Ollama, downloads a starter model and connects it.
Your subscription: click "Continue with ChatGPT" and sign in in your browser. Then turn on "Allow cloud AI for this company".
Click "Test connection". Ask AI and the automatic suggestions now use your model.

notes: With both set up, the local model answers first and ChatGPT takes over when it cannot.
Other services (Anthropic, Google Gemini, Groq, OpenRouter, Mistral, xAI, DeepSeek, Azure OpenAI, any OpenAI-compatible server) are under "Add AI…" with an API key, billed by that service per use.
A model on another computer of yours: "Find models on other computers (Tailscale)".

articles.title: What can I ask Ask AI?
articles.summary: Click Ask AI in the top bar and ask in plain words. It answers questions about your numbers from your own reports, tells you how to do something and links to the screen, and can draft an entry for you to approve. It never changes your books on its own.

steps.text: Numbers: "How did we do this month?", "Who owes us money?", "What is our cash balance?". Each figure names the report it came from.
How-to: "How do I reconcile my bank account?", "Where do I enter a bill?". The answer comes with a button that opens the screen.
Recording: "Record a $120 bill from Office Supply Co for supplies". It prepares a bill, invoice, payment or journal entry and shows it for you to Approve or Reject.

notes: Without a connected model Ask AI still gives basic answers from your reports and the built-in guide.
With a cloud model, listed names and identifiers are hidden before anything is sent.
asks: how do i use ask ai

articles.title: How do I let an AI agent work in my books?
articles.summary: An Admin adds the agent in Users & Roles > Agents, the way you would add a bookkeeper: a name, a role and what it may do without asking. Ironbooks then shows the agent's access token once, with the settings to paste into Claude Code or Claude Desktop.

steps.text: On the computer that holds the company file, open Users & Roles and click the Agents tab.
Click "New agent". Give it a Name: it is shown in the audit trail next to everything the agent does.
Tick a Role. The agent sees what a person with that role sees and can never ask for more. Choose the smallest role that does the job.

Under "What it may do without asking", keep "Ask for every change" unless you have a reason to change it: the agent then looks and prepares drafts by itself, and every change to the books waits for a person to say yes.
Leave "May work while nobody is signed in" off unless the agent must work when nobody is at the computer. Click "Make agent".
Copy what the next window shows: the Access token, and the line for Claude Code or the block for Claude Desktop. The token is shown only now. Keep it like a password, then click "I have copied it".
Paste the settings into Claude Code or Claude Desktop on this computer. The agent works while the company file is open here and someone has signed in. What it asks for waits in Agent requests.
To change what it may do later, click the agent in the list. "Pause this agent" stops it at once; Remove takes its access away for good.

notes: Only an Admin can add or remove an agent, or let one do more by itself. Whoever may change users can make an agent stricter, pause it, or revoke standing permission it was given.
An agent never changes its own settings or another agent's, never approves its own requests, and may not change or delete a role an agent holds.
What an agent reads is sent to the AI service that runs it. With an AI model on your own computer or network, nothing leaves.
Full Social Security and account numbers are never shown to an agent unless a person approves that one request. The Audit Trail says what was shown, to which agent, and who approved it.
A lost token cannot be shown again: remove the agent and make a new one. An Admin can stop every agent at once with "Pause all agents".
asks: let an agent do my bookkeeping
what can an agent do on its own

articles.title: How do I approve or deny what an agent asks to do?
articles.summary: What an agent's settings say to ask for waits in Agent requests. Open a request, check what Ironbooks worked out it would do, then choose "Approve once", "Approve similar…" or "Deny…".

steps.text: When an agent asks, a number shows on "Agent requests" in the left menu (in the desktop app, also at the top of the window).

Click Open on a request. The card shows the agent's reason in quotes (its own words, which Ironbooks has not checked) and what the request would do: the entries it would post, what it would change, any email, file or printing, and any warnings.
If it is right, click "Approve once". Ironbooks does it now, with your access.
To let the agent do requests like this one by itself for a while, click "Approve similar…", choose "For how long" and the limits under "Only when", then click "Approve this and similar".
If it is not right, click "Deny…", write a note for the agent if you like, and click "Deny request". Nothing is done.
Several requests of the same kind can be approved together: tick them, click "Approve chosen (…)…", check the list and the total it shows, and approve.

notes: "The books changed since the agent asked" means someone changed a record the request uses. The card shows what would happen now; approve it only if that is still right.

Standing permission lasts until the end of the day at most, and 30 minutes for emails and printing. It is never given for deleting, closed periods, settings, users, the company file, passwords or showing full numbers: those are asked one at a time.
Some requests need an Admin, a second person or a password; the card says so. A password typed on the card goes to Ironbooks only, never to the agent.
Requests approved together are added up per agent: when they pass the amount above which that agent needs two people, approve them one at a time.
Everything an agent did or asked is kept: see the Audit Trail, or Reports > Accountant & Taxes > Agent Activity.
asks: the agent is waiting for my approval
what does the books changed mean
give the agent permission for the rest of the day

articles.title: How do I let AI categorize bank transactions, and check what it did?
articles.summary: Ironbooks learns how you categorize. It can add the bank lines it is confident about on its own, and you can see and undo every one.

steps.text: Open AI & Automation. Under Automation, turn "Auto-categorize confident bank-feed transactions" on or off and set the Confidence threshold.
Open "What the AI posted" to see every line it added, and undo any of them.
Lines below the threshold wait for you in Review bank transactions.

articles.title: How do I have my books checked for mistakes?
articles.summary: Error Review looks for unbalanced, duplicate and miscategorized entries and other common problems, and explains how to fix each one.

steps.text: Open Error Review.
Open an issue to read the Analysis, the "Steps to resolve" and the "Impact if unresolved".
Fix it where it says, or apply the suggested correction when one is offered.

notes: Data Integrity proves the ledger itself balances: see "How do I check that my data is sound?".

articles.title: How do I enter things by typing a sentence?
articles.summary: Press Ctrl+K and type what you want, such as "invoice Acme 3 hours consulting". The form opens filled in for you to check. Nothing is saved without you.

steps.text: Press Ctrl+K anywhere.
Type the task: "invoice Acme 3 hours consulting", "show unpaid bills over 60 days", "what did we spend on fuel in Q3?".
Check the form that opens and save it yourself.

notes: Common phrases work with no AI model. Sentences the command bar does not recognize are passed to your connected model.
asks: type a sentence to create an invoice

articles.title: How do I move my books from QuickBooks Desktop?
articles.summary: Migrate from QuickBooks brings your books over in three steps: lists first, then history, then open invoices and bills.

steps.text: Open Migrate from QuickBooks (File > Migrate from QuickBooks…, or "Convert from QuickBooks…" on the start screen).
Step 1 · Chart of accounts and lists (IIF / CSV / Excel) — start here: export your lists from QuickBooks as IIF and import them.
Step 2 · History from your General Ledger: import a QuickBooks General Ledger report as PDF, Excel or CSV. It is checked to the penny against the trial balance before anything is saved.
Step 3 · Open invoices and unpaid bills: import them as real documents, so you can receive payments and pay bills on day one.
Payroll mid-year? Enter what was already paid this year in Payroll setup.

notes: Do the steps in order: history needs the accounts from Step 1.
Try the whole move on a copy first with "Try it on a copy".

articles.title: Where is the QuickBooks screen I am used to?
articles.summary: Every screen keeps its QuickBooks name for search, and the menus can show QuickBooks names. The QuickBooks keyboard shortcuts work too.

steps.text: Press Ctrl+K, or use the menu search box, and type the QuickBooks name: "Write Checks", "Memorized Transactions", "Finance Charges".
To have the menus use QuickBooks names, turn on "Use QuickBooks names in the menu" in My Preferences.
Press ? on any page for the shortcuts: Ctrl+W Write Checks, Ctrl+I Invoice, Ctrl+J Customer Center, Ctrl+A Chart of Accounts, Ctrl+R Register, Ctrl+F Find.

notes: docs/guide/quickbooks-names.md lists every QuickBooks screen name beside its Ironbooks screen.

articles.title: How do I get my data out of Ironbooks?
articles.summary: Lists and transactions export to IIF, CSV and Excel, and the whole ledger exports as an Excel workbook or PDF.

steps.text: Open Migrate from QuickBooks and use "Export lists and transactions".
For the ledger: File > Export Shareable Ledger, as an Excel Workbook (.xlsx) or a PDF Summary (.pdf).
The Chart of Accounts has its own "Export CSV".

articles.title: How do I fix a mistake?
articles.summary: Your books keep a permanent history, so mistakes are corrected rather than erased. Pick the case that fits.

steps.text: Just saved it? Click Undo on the message that appears: it works for 30 seconds after a save, void or delete.
Wrong amount, date, customer or account on an invoice, bill, check or receipt: open it from its list, change it and save. If it is linked to a payment or deposit, you may need to undo that first.
The transaction should never have happened: Void it. The amounts become zero but the record stays visible in the Audit Trail.
A payment went to the wrong invoice: open Receive Payments, void the payment, then record it again against the right invoice.
Money is in the wrong account: open the transaction and change the account, or for many at once use a journal entry.
Not sure what went wrong? Error Review looks for duplicates, out-of-balance entries and other common problems.

articles.title: Why can’t I change a transaction with an old date?
articles.summary: The books are closed through a closing date. Transactions dated on or before it cannot be added, changed or voided without the closing date password.

steps.text: Enter the closing date password when asked, if you have it.
Or record the correction with a date after the closing date.
An Admin can change or remove the closing date in Preferences ("Set Closing Date"), or reopen a closed period.

notes: Ask your accountant before changing a closed period: it changes numbers they may already have reported.
asks: date is in a closed period

articles.title: How do I check that my data is sound?
articles.summary: Data Integrity proves that debits equal credits, the balance sheet balances and every account balance matches the ledger.

steps.text: Open Data Integrity. The checks run on their own.
If a check fails, click "Preview Rebuild" to see what would change, then "Rebuild".

notes: Make a backup before a rebuild.

articles.title: How do I merge duplicate customers, vendors or accounts?
articles.summary: Merge Duplicates moves everything from one record to another and deactivates the one you no longer want.

steps.text: Open Merge Records and choose the Record Type.
Pick "From (will be deactivated)" and "To (master record)", then confirm with "Yes, Merge".

notes: A merge cannot be undone. Back up first.
asks: i have the same vendor twice

screens.label: Home
screens.what: Your starting point: "Needs attention" lists what is waiting on you, most urgent first; "Overview" shows how money moves, and you click any step to do it.
screens.first: Work down Needs attention, or on Overview pick a task such as Create Invoices or Pay Bills.

screens.label: Needs attention
screens.what: Everything waiting on you, most urgent first: bank transactions to sort, late customers, bills due, reconciling, payroll taxes, to-dos and backups.
screens.first: Use the button on each line (Sort it, Send reminder, Pay, Done). Not now? Choose Later to snooze or dismiss it.

screens.label: Agent requests
screens.what: On its own an agent does only what its settings allow, usually looking and drafting; what it must ask for waits here, showing the change. The Audit Trail and Agent Activity report keep the record.
screens.first: Approve once, Approve similar… (standing permission) or Deny. Whoever manages users can pause an agent; an Admin can pause all.

screens.label: To Do list
screens.what: Calls, emails, meetings and tasks you want to remember, optionally about a customer, vendor, employee or lead. They also show on the Calendar and in Reminders.
screens.first: Click "New to-do", describe it and pick a due date.

screens.label: Invoices
screens.what: Bill a customer who will pay you later. Saving an invoice records the sale and what the customer owes you.
screens.first: Click "New invoice", pick the customer, add what you sold and save.

screens.label: Sales Receipts
screens.what: Record a sale that was paid on the spot (cash, card or check), so no invoice is needed.
screens.first: Click "New sales receipt", pick the customer, add what you sold and how they paid.

screens.label: Estimates
screens.what: A price quote for a customer. It does not change your books until you turn it into an invoice.
screens.first: Click "New estimate", add the work or items, then send it to the customer.

screens.label: Sales Orders
screens.what: Track an order a customer placed that you will deliver and invoice later. It does not change your books by itself.
screens.first: Click "New sales order", add the items, and invoice it when you ship.

screens.label: Sales order fulfillment
screens.what: See which open sales orders you can ship now with the stock on hand.
screens.first: Tick the orders to fill, then print pick lists or create the invoices.

screens.label: Receive Payments
screens.what: Record money a customer paid you against their invoices, so their balance goes down.
screens.first: Pick the customer, enter the amount, and tick the invoices it pays.

screens.label: Credit Memos
screens.what: Give a customer a credit (for a return or a mistake) that lowers what they owe, or refund them.
screens.first: Click "New credit memo", pick the customer and add what you are crediting. Prices follow the price level set on the customer.

screens.label: Customers
screens.what: Everyone you sell to, with their contact details, balance owed and history.
screens.first: Click "New customer" to add one, or click a name to see what they owe.

screens.label: Leads
screens.what: People who might become customers. Track calls and to-dos, then turn a lead into a customer in one click.
screens.first: Add a lead, then add a to-do to follow up.

screens.label: Late-payment charges
screens.what: Add interest or a late fee to customers whose invoices are overdue.
screens.first: Check the rate and grace period, review the list, then assess the charges you want.

screens.label: Money coming in
screens.what: One view of estimates, unbilled orders, unbilled time and costs, open and overdue invoices, and money paid in the last 30 days.
screens.first: Click a coloured bar to see those transactions; use a row’s action to receive a payment or bill time and costs.

screens.label: Collect overdue payments
screens.what: Customers who are late paying, with how much and how late, so you can follow up.
screens.first: On a customer, log a call, email the overdue invoices or a statement, print a collection letter, or receive a payment.

screens.label: Invoice many customers
screens.what: Send the same charge (for example a monthly fee) to a group of customers in one go.
screens.first: Pick the customers (or a saved Billing Group), add the items once, then create the invoices.

screens.label: Items
screens.what: The products and services you buy and sell. Each item knows its price and which account it goes to.
screens.first: Click "New item" and add the things you sell most.

screens.label: Sales Reps
screens.what: The people credited with sales, so reports can show sales by rep.
screens.first: Add each rep once, then pick them on invoices.

screens.label: Pricing rules
screens.what: Automatic price changes, for example 10% off for a customer group or a sale price for a date range.
screens.first: Click "New rule", choose who and what it applies to, and the price change.

screens.label: Purchase Orders
screens.what: An order you send a vendor. It does not change your books until the items arrive or the bill comes.
screens.first: Click "New purchase order", pick the vendor and the items you are ordering.

screens.label: Receive Items
screens.what: Record items that arrived before the bill, so your stock is right.
screens.first: Pick the vendor and the purchase order, then enter what arrived.

screens.label: Bill for received items
screens.what: When the bill comes for items you already received, turn that receipt into a bill.
screens.first: Pick the vendor and the item receipt, check the amounts and save.

screens.label: Enter Bills
screens.what: Record a bill you received and will pay later, so you know what you owe each vendor.
screens.first: Click "New bill", pick the vendor, the amount and what it was for.

screens.label: Pay Bills
screens.what: Pay the bills you already entered. Each payment lowers what you owe the vendor.
screens.first: Tick the bills to pay, choose the bank account and payment date, then pay.

screens.label: Write Checks
screens.what: Record money you paid right away by check, debit card or cash, and what it was for.
screens.first: Click "New check", pick the bank account, the payee and the expense. The payee can be a vendor or someone on the Other Names list.

screens.label: Receipts
screens.what: Photos and PDFs of receipts waiting to be entered. Ironbooks reads them on this computer and fills in a new expense or bill for you to check.
screens.first: Drag a receipt anywhere in the app, or click Add receipts or Send from your phone.

screens.label: Vendor Credits
screens.what: A credit from a vendor (for a return or overcharge) that lowers what you owe them.
screens.first: Click "New vendor credit", pick the vendor and the amount; use it when you pay bills.

screens.label: Pay Sales Tax
screens.what: See the sales tax you collected and owe each tax agency, and pay it.
screens.first: Pick the bank account and the "show tax due through" date, tick the agencies to pay, then pay.

screens.label: Print Checks
screens.what: Print the checks you marked "to be printed" on your check stock.
screens.first: Pick the bank account and starting check number, then print. Answer "Did checks print OK?" to record check numbers.

screens.label: Vendors
screens.what: Everyone you buy from, with their details, balance you owe and history.
screens.first: Click "New vendor" to add one, or click a name to see open bills.

screens.label: Bank accounts
screens.what: Your bank and credit card accounts with their balances.
screens.first: Click an account to see its transactions, or add a new account.

screens.label: Registers
screens.what: Every transaction in one account, like a checkbook, with a running balance.
screens.first: Pick an account to open its register.

screens.label: Bank Feeds
screens.what: Bring in transactions from statement files your bank gives you, so you do not type them.
screens.first: Import the file from your bank, then review each line.

screens.label: Review bank transactions
screens.what: Match each imported bank line to a transaction you entered, or add it.
screens.first: Work down the list: confirm the suggested match or choose a category.

screens.label: Bank rules
screens.what: Rules tell the app which account to use for bank lines that look alike, such as every SHELL OIL charge going to Fuel. It also offers rules when you repeat a choice.
screens.first: Click "New rule", say what the bank line contains and which account it goes to, then test it.

screens.label: Make Deposits
screens.what: Group customer payments you took to the bank into one deposit, so it matches your bank statement.
screens.first: Tick the payments you deposited, choose the bank account and save.

screens.label: Reconcile
screens.what: Check your books against your bank statement so you know every transaction is right.
screens.first: Pick the account, enter the statement date and ending balance, then tick what cleared.

screens.label: Transfer Funds
screens.what: Move money between your own accounts, for example checking to savings.
screens.first: Pick the from and to accounts and the amount.

screens.label: Loans
screens.what: Track loans you owe, their payments and how much is interest. The balance owed is read from the loan account; "What if" compares another rate, payment or term, a lump sum or extra principal.
screens.first: Add a loan with its amount, rate and term (tick "already being paid" if you have been paying it). Then set up each payment.

screens.label: Enter many transactions
screens.what: Type or paste lots of checks, deposits, card charges, bills, invoices or journal entries in one spreadsheet-style grid. Each row is checked as you go and saved as its own transaction.
screens.first: Pick the transaction type, then type rows or paste them from Excel or Google Sheets. Fix rows marked red, then save.

screens.label: Journal entries
screens.what: Move amounts between accounts directly. Mostly used by accountants for adjustments.
screens.first: Ask your accountant before using it; debits must equal credits.

screens.label: Chart of Accounts
screens.what: The categories your money is sorted into: bank accounts, income, expenses, what you own and owe.
screens.first: Look through the list; add an account only when you need a new category.

screens.label: Pay payroll taxes
screens.what: Send the payroll taxes you withheld and owe to the government.
screens.first: Pick the date range, tick what you are paying and choose the bank account.

screens.label: Employees & payroll
screens.what: Your employees, their pay rates and tax settings.
screens.first: Add each employee, then run payroll.

screens.label: Run payroll
screens.what: Pay your employees: work out each paycheck, the taxes withheld and what you owe the government.
screens.first: Pick the pay period and employees, check the paychecks, then create them.

screens.label: Sales tax items
screens.what: The sales tax rates you charge and the tax agency each one is paid to. Inactive items stay on old sales but are not offered on new ones.
screens.first: Click "New sales tax item", give it a name and a rate, and pick (or add) its tax agency.

screens.label: Recurring transactions
screens.what: Transactions you enter again and again (rent, subscriptions), saved so they repeat on schedule or with one click.
screens.first: Save a transaction as recurring from its form, then set how often.

screens.label: Report Center
screens.what: Every report in one place: profit, what you own and owe, sales, spending, taxes and more.
screens.first: Start with Profit & Loss and Balance Sheet; click any report to open it.

screens.label: Profit & Loss
screens.what: Money in minus money out for a period: did the business make or lose money?
screens.first: Choose the dates at the top; click any amount to see the transactions behind it.

screens.label: Balance Sheet
screens.what: What the business owns, what it owes, and what is left over for the owners, on one date.
screens.first: Pick the date at the top; click any amount to see the details.

screens.label: Commented reports
screens.what: Reports saved with your comments on their amounts, kept exactly as they were when you commented them, to print, export or discuss later.
screens.first: On any report click "Comment on report", click the amounts to explain, then save. Open one here to change or export it.

screens.label: Close the month
screens.what: A guided checklist for the end of each month: reconcile, tidy up, review balances, then lock the books.
screens.first: Pick the month, work through each step, then close the books and download the report pack.

screens.label: Accountant's Copy
screens.what: Your accountant fixes anything dated on or before a dividing date while you keep working after it. Then you review their changes and import them.
screens.first: Pick the dividing date and create the copy. When the changes file comes back, open it here, check each change, then import.

screens.label: Reminders
screens.what: Everything that needs attention: overdue invoices, bills to pay, checks to print, money to deposit and to-dos.
screens.first: Click a line to go straight to the screen that handles it.

screens.label: Calendar
screens.what: A day, week or month view of entries, due dates (invoices, bills) and to-dos, with an Upcoming & Past Due list.
screens.first: Click a day to see or add what is on it. Preferences > Calendar sets the starting view and how far the list looks.

screens.label: Back Up & Restore
screens.quickbooks: Back Up Company / Restore Previous Local Backup
screens.what: Keeps safe copies of your company file, automatically on a schedule and whenever you ask. Look inside any copy before you restore it.
screens.first: Check the automatic backup schedule, then click "Back up now" to make a copy today.

screens.label: Try it on a copy
screens.menu: Setup › Try it on a copy
screens.what: Opens a throwaway copy of your whole company file so you can practice or test a change. Emails, bank feeds and automatic backups are off there.
screens.first: Click "Try it on a copy". When done, discard the copy or keep it as a training file.

screens.label: Period Copy
screens.what: A separate copy of your company file that shows only one period, for an auditor: opening balances for everything before it and nothing after it. Your own file is not changed.
screens.first: Pick the first and last day of the period and click "Create Period Copy".

screens.label: Users & Roles
screens.what: Who can sign in to this company file and what each person may do. A role sets access per activity, such as Invoices or Receive Payments.
screens.first: Add a user and give them one or more roles, or clone a built-in role to make your own.

screens.label: View Permissions
screens.what: Reports of what each role or user may do in every area and activity, side by side, plus the user and role lists.
screens.first: Pick a report, tick the roles or users to compare, then print it or download it as CSV.

screens.label: Security (2FA)
screens.what: Protects the company file with its own passwords: it is encrypted, and only its user names and passwords (or its recovery key) open it, on any computer.
screens.first: An Admin clicks "Protect This Company File with Passwords", then prints or saves the recovery key.

screens.label: Change My Password
screens.what: Choose a new password for signing in, following the password rules an Admin set under Users & Roles. When your password expires, you come here first.
screens.first: Type your current password, then the new one twice, and click Change password.

screens.label: Preferences
screens.what: Settings for the whole company and just for you, such as features you use, the menu style and the mail server that sends your forms (Send Forms).
screens.first: Open a category on the left, change what you need and save. Each category has a My Preferences and a Company Preferences tab.

screens.label: My Preferences
screens.what: Your own settings, open to every user: the name and email address your forms are sent from, Bcc me, menus and more.
screens.first: Pick a category on the left, change what you need and save. Only you are affected.

screens.label: System Accounts
screens.quickbooks: Accounts Ironbooks posts to (A/P, Inventory, COGS, Sales Tax, Payroll)
screens.what: The accounts Ironbooks posts to on its own: Accounts Payable, Inventory, Cost of Goods Sold, Sales Tax and Payroll Liabilities. A converted QuickBooks file may number them differently.
screens.first: Check the account each line posts to. If one is wrong, choose the right account and click Save.

screens.label: Setup Interview
screens.what: Answer a few questions about your company and the app turns on only the features you use.
screens.first: Fill in your company details, pick your tax form, then choose the features. You can skip any time.

screens.label: What's behind this number
screens.what: Every transaction that adds up to the amount you clicked on a report, using the same dates, basis and filters as the report.
screens.first: Click a date to open that transaction and its original document; use Back to return to the report where you left it.

screens.label: Sign in
screens.what: Opens the company file with your user name and password. A protected company file is unlocked on this computer by this same sign-in.
screens.first: Type your password and press Enter. Forgot it? Choose "I forgot my password", or use the recovery key.

screens.label: Help & Glossary
screens.what: Plain-language guides for common tasks and a glossary of accounting terms.
screens.first: Type what you want to do in the search box.

glossary.short: Money customers owe you. When you send an invoice, the amount goes into A/R until the customer pays.
glossary.long: Example: you invoice a customer $500 today with 30-day terms. Your income is recorded now, and the $500 sits in A/R. When the customer pays, use Receive Payments — the $500 moves out of A/R and into your bank (or Undeposited Funds).

glossary.short: Money you owe vendors. When you enter a bill, the amount goes into A/P until you pay it.
glossary.long: Example: your supplier sends a $300 bill due next month. Enter Bills records the expense now and puts $300 in A/P. When you pay it with Pay Bills, A/P goes down and so does your bank balance.

glossary.short: A holding spot for payments you have received but not yet taken to the bank. Use Record Deposits to move them into your bank account.
glossary.long: Like the envelope of checks in your drawer. Grouping them into one deposit means your books show the same single deposit your bank statement shows, which makes reconciling easy.

glossary.short: Income counts when you invoice and expenses count when you get the bill — even if no money has moved yet.
glossary.long: Accrual shows what you earned and owe in a period, which gives a truer picture of profit. Most growing businesses and all businesses with inventory use it.

glossary.short: Income counts when the money arrives and expenses count when you pay them.
glossary.long: Cash basis is simpler and matches your bank account. You can record everything normally and still switch any report between cash and accrual.

glossary.short: Two ways to time your reports. Accrual counts sales when you invoice; cash counts them when you get paid. Your records are the same either way — only the report view changes.
An optional tag for tracking parts of your business — such as locations, departments or product lines — so you can see profit for each one.
glossary.long: Example: a bakery with two shops can tag every sale and expense with "Downtown" or "Uptown" and then run Profit & Loss by Class.

glossary.short: A lock on your books. Transactions dated on or before the closing date cannot be changed without the closing-date password.
glossary.long: Set it after you file taxes or finish a year so nobody accidentally changes numbers you already reported.

glossary.short: Checking your books against your bank or credit card statement, line by line, so you know both agree.
glossary.long: Each month, enter the statement ending balance, tick off every transaction that appears on the statement, and finish when the difference is 0.00. Anything left over is a mistake or something the bank has not processed yet.

glossary.short: Every transaction touches at least two accounts: one side is the debit, the other the credit, and the two must always be equal. That rule is what keeps your books in balance.
glossary.long: Debits increase what you own (assets) and your expenses. Credits increase what you owe (liabilities), owner equity and income. You rarely need to think about this — invoices, bills and checks pick the right side for you. It matters only for journal entries.

glossary.short: Profit from earlier years that is still in the business. At the start of each fiscal year, last year’s profit (or loss) moves here automatically.
A temporary account that balances your books when you enter starting balances. Once setup is finished it should be zero — your accountant moves what is left into owner’s equity.
A manual transaction where you choose the accounts and the debit and credit amounts yourself. Usually used for adjustments and corrections — everyday work has its own forms.
The list of categories your money is sorted into: bank accounts, what you own, what you owe, income and expenses.
Recording money you took to the bank. Pick the payments waiting in Undeposited Funds so your deposit matches the bank statement.
Tax you collect from customers on behalf of the government. It is not your income — it is held in Sales Tax Payable until you pay it to the tax agency.
Payroll taxes and withholdings you have taken out of paychecks (or owe as the employer) but have not yet paid to the government.
Your business’s 12-month accounting year. Most businesses use January to December, but it can start in any month.
Cancelling a transaction while keeping a record of it. The amounts become zero, but the transaction stays visible in the audit trail.
The final balance printed on your bank or credit card statement for the period you are reconciling.
Tells the books what kind of account this is — a bank account, money customers owe you, a bill you owe, income, an expense and so on. It decides where the account appears on your reports.
glossary.long: Example: prepaid insurance is something you own but cannot spend, so it is an Other Current Asset, not a Bank account. A loan you repay over five years is a Long Term Liability.

glossary.short: An account that only keeps track of estimates, sales orders or purchase orders. Nothing in it is real money yet, so it never appears on your financial reports.
A journal entry made at the end of a period to correct or update the books — for example recording depreciation or expenses you owe but have not been billed for yet.
The line on your business income-tax return that an account adds up to. Setting it lets your tax preparer pull the right totals straight from your books.
The customer, vendor or employee a journal entry line is for. Lines that touch Accounts Receivable need a customer, and lines that touch Accounts Payable need a vendor, so their balances stay right.
A charge you add straight to the balance a customer owes instead of sending a separate invoice. It shows up on their next statement and in A/R aging.
glossary.long: Example: you bill a monthly $50 service fee. Enter it as a statement charge, and it appears on their monthly statement with everything else they owe.

glossary.short: A customer check the bank returned unpaid, usually for "non-sufficient funds". Recording it takes the money back out of your bank and puts the amount back on what the customer owes.
glossary.long: Example: a customer pays a $200 invoice by check and you deposit it. A week later the bank returns it. Record Bounced Check reopens the invoice, takes $200 out of the bank, and can add the bank fee as an expense and charge the customer a returned-check fee.

glossary.short: A reduction you give a customer for paying before a set date, such as 2% off if paid within 10 days ("2% 10, Net 30").
glossary.long: Example: an invoice of $1,000 has terms 2% 10, Net 30. If the customer pays within 10 days they pay $980; in Receive Payments you apply $980 of cash plus a $20 discount, and the invoice is paid in full.
